title: I made an AI streamer who plays my racing game 24/7 (well, it could) on YouTube
author: nicotinum
selftext:
Nico plays my game Spino Ghost Racing live on YouTube, around the clock: he races, browses tracks, builds his own and talks to chat.



Gemini models:

\- gemini-3.8-live: his voice, with a screenshot of the game every line. About $0.82 an hour (half a cent a line).

\- gemini-3.1-flash-lite: chat moderation, checking his promises, memory notes. About $0.04 an hour.

\- gemini-embedding-2: long-term memory, so he doesn't repeat himself. Under $0.01 an hour.

\- Lyria 3.5: the music, 18 loops for about $1.50, once.



Total: about $0.85 an hour.



Live now: [https://youtube.com/live/uLWjJD7OH0s](https://youtube.com/live/uLWjJD7OH0s)

  
Have any of you had tried something like this (some ready-to-use service)? Could it be possible to get exposure like this?

comments.author: Rsouss
comments.body: Great project, can it play other games or just that one?

replies.author: nicotinum
replies.body:
Thanks! Just this one for now. It runs inside my game's code (Godot), presses the "real" buttons and uses the game's own autopilot to drive, so another game would need that part rebuilt.

I guess some simple puzzle games could be done ...

comments.author: bigorangemachine
comments.body: That's fun.  I'm actually hoping to vibe code a game that interacts live chat... we got some overlap lol

comments.author: MC897
comments.body: What a fantastic idea. Does it make championships and customise cars too etc? Giving the game depth would give the streamer more interesting outputs too

replies.author: nicotinum
replies.body: thanks! at the moment it just makes test tracks and drives them sometimes. or explores the championship creator. i designed it to not publish anything yet - aiming the content in the game to be still fully players made.

replies.author: nicotinum
replies.body: oh yeah it sometimes customizes his car!
